title: Approval Ratings Presentation
text: A pollster presents sixty slides of approval data. Every chart slopes the same way, and a staffer has labeled the axis "Winning, mostly."

options.label: Read every slide
options.result: You studied the charts. The pollster was asked to leave the room when you asked whether the Y axis could be moved.

ignore.text: The polling deck went unread. The numbers carried on without your input.

inspiredBy: Reports of low approval ratings in polls through 2025 and 2026.

title: Press Credential Policy Briefing
text: Lawyers walk you through a 20-page press credential pledge. Most reporters declined to sign it, which leaves a lot of empty chairs to discuss.

options.label: Review the pledge
options.result: You reviewed the pledge. The empty briefing-room chairs are now described as "streamlined."

ignore.text: The credential policy sat in a drawer. A new reporter tried signing it with a crayon.

inspiredBy: Defense Department press credential rules that major outlets refused to sign, October 2025.

title: Public Broadcasting Wind-Down Memo
text: A memo explains what happens to local stations after federal funding ends. It has a section on puppets and you are asked to read it twice.

options.label: Read the whole memo
options.result: You read the memo. A station manager in a small town is now your most thoughtful correspondent.

ignore.text: The memo was unread. A children's program ended on a cliffhanger.

inspiredBy: Congress canceled public broadcasting funding and the corporation began winding down, mid-2025.

title: Social Media Analytics Review
text: Staff present a report on which of your posts did best. Posts about posting did best. Posts about policy did slightly worse than a weather alert.

options.label: Study the report
options.result: You learned that policy posts underperform. You asked if the policy could be less policy.

ignore.text: The analytics report went unread, so your next post will be chosen by instinct again.

inspiredBy: Debate over the volume and content of presidential social media posting, 2025.

title: Fifteen Billion Dollar Complaint
text: Lawyers propose suing a big newspaper for defamation. The first filing was returned by a judge for being too long and too angry.

options.label: Ask lawyers for a short version
options.result: The lawyers cut it to a reasonable length. Several adjectives did not survive.

options.label: File it at full length
options.result: You filed the 85-page version. It ran longer than the paper's coverage you disliked.

ignore.text: The suit sat unfiled. The newspaper ran another article and nobody sued.

inspiredBy: Trump sued a major newspaper for about $15 billion; a judge struck the first complaint, September 2025.

title: Birthday Letter Lawsuit
text: A financial paper has published a story about a birthday letter you say you never wrote. Lawyers say suing means answering questions under oath.

options.label: Skip the lawsuit
options.result: You let it pass. Your lawyer sighed with relief and ordered a very large lunch.

options.label: Sue for ten billion
options.result: You sued for ten billion. Discovery now requires you to find a birthday letter.

ignore.text: The story kept circulating. The letter has still not been located.

inspiredBy: Trump sued a financial newspaper over a reported birthday letter, July 2025.

title: Sue the Pollster
text: A poll showed you trailing in a state you won. Lawyers say there is a legal theory that polls are consumer fraud, though not a good one.

options.label: Accept the poll
options.result: You accepted the poll. The pollster has been invited to nothing, as usual.

options.label: Sue the pollster
options.result: You sued the pollster. The poll is now the most famous poll in the country.

ignore.text: The poll stood. A second poll came out confirming the first.

inspiredBy: Lawsuit over a 2024 Iowa poll against a newspaper and its pollster.

title: Press Pool Seating Chart
text: Staff ask who should sit in the pool. The traditional list includes a wire service that refuses to use a name you gave a body of water.

options.label: Restore the traditional pool
options.result: The pool was restored. The wire service arrived with a very large map.

options.label: Seat only friendly outlets
options.result: The pool now contains six supportive streamers and a man filming his own lunch.

ignore.text: The seating chart stayed blank. Reporters stood and the Oval Office grew crowded.

inspiredBy: White House restricted a wire service from pool spaces over the Gulf of America naming dispute, 2025.

title: Take Over the Pool Schedule
text: The press association has traditionally chosen who joins the pool. You can now choose yourself, which would be your favorite kind of chart.

options.label: Leave the schedule alone
options.result: You left it alone. The association kept scheduling, and no one was more bored than you.

options.label: Run the schedule yourself
options.result: You now pick who asks questions. Every question is about how well you are doing.

ignore.text: The pool schedule stayed with the association. They invited the whole building.

inspiredBy: White House took control of press pool composition from the correspondents' association, February 2025.

title: Settle With the Network
text: A network offers to settle a lawsuit about an interview edit for millions. Your lawyers note they would also like an apology, which is tricky for you.

options.label: Accept the plain settlement
options.result: You took the money. Nobody was thanked and everyone moved on.

options.label: Demand a public apology too
options.result: You asked for an apology. The network offered a statement with the word "regret" next to "scheduling."

ignore.text: The settlement offer expired. Lawyers billed you for the time.

inspiredBy: A network settled a lawsuit over an interview edit for $16 million, 2025.

title: Cut an International Broadcaster
text: A government broadcaster sends news abroad in dozens of languages. A memo suggests ending it, and replacing it with one channel playing you.

options.label: Keep a lean version
options.result: You kept a lean version. The foreign-language announcers continue reading the weather.

options.label: Replace it with You TV
options.result: Your channel now airs in fifty languages. Viewers gave it solid ratings in six.

ignore.text: The funding question stayed open. The broadcaster kept broadcasting, to your irritation.

inspiredBy: Administration moves to shut down a government-funded international broadcaster, 2025.

title: Post the Papal Image
text: An AI image shows you dressed as a pope. Staff say it is probably okay to post. A Cardinal says it is probably not.

options.label: Do not post it
options.result: You did not post it. The image remains in your phone as a prayer.

options.label: Post it anyway
options.result: You posted it. Several billion Catholics and one Cardinal gave their reviews.

ignore.text: The image sat in drafts and a staffer posted it from their own account.

inspiredBy: Trump shared an AI image of himself dressed as pope, May 2025.

title: The Approval Number
text: A new poll puts your approval at 41 percent. A reporter reads the number aloud, slowly, as if it were a diagnosis.

options.label: Say polls go up and down
options.result: You said polls go up and down. This one stayed where it was, but everyone moved on.

options.label: Announce your own poll
options.result: Your poll has you at 104 percent. The pollster is you. The margin of error is zero.

ignore.text: You left the number unanswered. It was shown on a loop, with a downward arrow.

inspiredBy: Recurring 2025 approval polling and the president disputing unfavorable polls.

title: Late-Night Host Monologue
text: A late-night host has made a joke about you. You were not named but you recognized yourself, as one does.

options.label: Let the joke go
options.result: You said nothing. The host ran out of material by Thursday.

options.label: Demand he be fired
options.result: You demanded his firing. The ratings of his show tripled.

ignore.text: You said nothing, then eight million people repeated the joke for you.

inspiredBy: Late-night host suspension and return after FCC chair comments, September 2025.

title: Late-Night Show Canceled
text: A major late-night show has been canceled. Reporters ask whether you had anything to do with it, which you did not and want credit for.

options.label: Say it was a business decision
options.result: You said it was business. A network executive nodded from a hiding place.

options.label: Claim victory publicly
options.result: You took credit. Their lawyers asked you to stop helping.

ignore.text: You said nothing. The host's farewell special was seen by everyone.

inspiredBy: CBS canceled The Late Show; Trump celebrated on social media, July 2025.

title: Sunday Interview
text: A major newsmagazine wants an interview. They will edit it, which as you know is where the crimes happen.

options.label: Do it live, no edits
options.result: You went live. It was fine, which is the most annoying result.

options.label: Demand final cut
options.result: You demanded final cut. The producer asked what he was cutting from.

ignore.text: The interview was declined. A guest chair stayed empty on Sunday night.

inspiredBy: Trump's dispute and settlement with a network over edit of an interview, 2024-2025.

title: Crowd Size Question
text: A reporter asks about turnout at your military parade. Aerial photographs exist and are not helpful to your side.

options.label: Say attendance was fine
options.result: You said it was a solid turnout. The photographs agreed, mostly.

options.label: Claim it was historic
options.result: You called it the biggest ever. Several photographers have a lot to say about it.

ignore.text: The question hung in the air. A drone provided the answer later.

inspiredBy: Disputes over crowd sizes at Trump's military parade, June 2025.

title: AI Video Question
text: A reporter asks about an AI video you posted of a jet dropping something unpleasant on protesters. A staffer says it is "satire."

options.label: Say you did not review it
options.result: You said staff posted it. Staff said it was you. It was you.

options.label: Defend it as great
options.result: You defended the video. The video now has a sequel and a director.

ignore.text: The question went unanswered. The video was shown on every channel, free.

inspiredBy: Trump posted an AI video of a jet dumping on protesters after No Kings rallies, October 2025.

title: Ratings Question
text: A reporter asks about your policy agenda. You would rather discuss how many people watched your last speech.

options.label: Talk about policy
options.result: You discussed policy. Your ratings fell to your own satisfaction, but only by a little.

options.label: Quote the ratings
options.result: You cited the ratings. The reporter checked and they were the second-highest in history.

ignore.text: You never answered. The reporter wrote the numbers up for you.

inspiredBy: Trump's frequent references to TV ratings for himself and allies, 2025.

title: Nickname Round
text: A reporter asks about a rival. You have a new nickname ready. It rhymes with nothing but you are sure it is working.

options.label: Use his actual name
options.result: You used his name. The room paused to see whether this was a trap.

options.label: Deploy the nickname
options.result: You rolled out the nickname. It took six tries to pronounce.

ignore.text: You never answered. The nickname leaked anyway, in the first person.

inspiredBy: Trump's habit of giving critics and rivals nicknames in 2025.

title: Empty Briefing Seats
text: Most reporters walked out of the Pentagon rather than sign your pledge. A reporter asks if anyone remains.

options.label: Say you will talk to them
options.result: You offered talks. The reporters were polite and kept their umbrellas.

options.label: Say the press is replaced
options.result: You announced a new press corps. It consisted of five podcasters and an inflatable.

ignore.text: No one answered. The seats stayed empty and so did the scheduling.

inspiredBy: Dozens of reporters surrendered Pentagon credentials rather than sign a policy, October 2025.

title: Documentary Edit Question
text: A broadcaster edited two parts of your speech into one. A reporter asks whether you want an apology or a billion dollars.

options.label: Accept the apology
options.result: You took the apology. The executive offered a second one, in case.

options.label: Ask for the billion
options.result: You asked for a billion dollars. The broadcaster's lawyer asked whether you meant pounds.

ignore.text: You said nothing. A broadcasting chief resigned anyway and you took the credit.

inspiredBy: Trump threatened a lawsuit over a documentary that edited his speech; BBC leaders resigned, November 2025.

title: Sleepy Event Question
text: A reporter asks whether you dozed off during an event. Photographs show closed eyes and a very open mouth.

options.label: Say you were resting
options.result: You said you were resting your eyes. The photographer said they were very rested.

options.label: Say you were blinking
options.result: You said it was long blinking. The photographers called this a new record.

ignore.text: You ignored the question. The photo spent the week on the front page.

inspiredBy: Reports and photos of Trump appearing to nod off at public events, 2025.

title: New Media Seat Question
text: A reporter asks why the briefing room has chairs for podcasters and none for the old guard. Your press secretary says it is "diversity."

options.label: Expand the room
options.result: You added chairs. The room is now a very cheerful, very crowded place.

options.label: Stay with the influencers
options.result: You kept the influencers. Their first question was about your hair.

ignore.text: You never explained the seating. Fifty chairs arrived unannounced.

inspiredBy: White House gave briefing room seats to new media and podcasters, 2025.

title: Fact-Check Moment
text: A reporter points out that a number you gave on stage is off by a factor of ten.

options.label: Correct the number
options.result: You corrected it. The room applauded politely and then looked at their phones.

options.label: Insist it is right
options.result: You doubled down. The number has since been increased to be consistent.

ignore.text: You said nothing. The correction went out on the news and the chart.

inspiredBy: Trump's public statements frequently drew fact-checks from reporters during 2025.

title: The Broadcast License Call
text: The communications regulator calls. A network aired something unkind, and he is wondering about licenses. He would like you to be impressed.

options.label: Stay out of it
options.result: You said regulators are independent. The regulator said "of course" and meant "wink."

options.label: Encourage the threat
options.result: You told him to look into it. He said he already had, which you had not known.

ignore.text: The call went to voicemail. The regulator tweeted about it anyway.

inspiredBy: FCC chair threatened broadcasters over content, with license remarks and presidential support, 2025.

title: The Merger Call
text: A media owner calls about a merger that needs approval. He mentions that his news division is "reviewing its tone."

options.label: Say it goes through the process
options.result: You stayed out of it. The owner said "of course" and went to rework his news.

options.label: Hint at a news anchor change
options.result: You mentioned an anchor. The owner wrote it down.

ignore.text: The call went unreturned. The merger was approved and you took the credit.

inspiredBy: Media mergers requiring federal approval amid pressure on news divisions, 2025.

title: The Editor Calls Back
text: A newspaper editor calls after a story you disliked. She offers a correction, which would be a historic first for your desk.

options.label: Take the correction
options.result: You took it. The correction was small and so were your complaints.

options.label: Ask for the front page
options.result: You asked for a front-page apology. She said the front page was "full."

ignore.text: You did not return the call. The editor ran the story with a clarifying note.

inspiredBy: Disputes with newspapers over corrections and lawsuits, 2025.

title: The Press Secretary Calls
text: Your press secretary calls at 6 a.m. about the fourteen posts you sent overnight. Three have typos and one has a hat.

options.label: Delete a few posts
options.result: You deleted four posts. The press secretary sent flowers, a note, and a replacement phone.

options.label: Post more
options.result: You posted nine more. The press secretary now speaks in a calm, slow voice.

ignore.text: You ignored the call. The posts remained, and so did her sigh.

inspiredBy: Trump's overnight bursts of dozens of social posts, reported through 2025.

title: Approval Rating Question
text: A reporter reads out a poll showing your approval at a new low and asks what you make of it. Staff signal that "fake" is not an answer.

options.label: Say you hear the concern
options.result: You said you heard the concern. A staffer fainted, then recovered.

options.label: Cite your private polls
options.result: You said your own polls show 95 percent. The pollster turned out to be a golf friend.

ignore.text: The question went unanswered. The poll was then read out again, slower.

inspiredBy: Polls showing Trump approval ratings at second-term lows, 2025-2026.
